title: Use Explore to query data without building a dashboard

blocks.content:
Picture this. A teammate asks you if a service really got slower after yesterday's release. No dashboard shows that exact number, and it isn't worth building one for a question you'll ask once.

It isn't a job for Drilldown either. Drilldown is for investigating when you don't yet know what you're looking for, and here the question is already precise. You just need the answer. Explore is the page for that. Pick a data source, run a query, read the chart, then adjust and run again until you see what you need.

In this guide you'll load a real query against a demo system's data.

Click **Explore** in the main menu.

Unlike a dashboard, this page isn't something other people look at. It's your own workspace, and queries you run here don't change any dashboard or affect anyone else.
That's Explore. One page for asking your data a direct question, with nothing to set up first.
Next, read the page from top to bottom.

Notice the **data source** picker.

It chooses where the query runs. A data source is a connection to a place that already holds your data. To answer your teammate, you'd pick the one that collects the service's response times.
blocks.tooltip: Every query runs against one of your connected data stores. This picker chooses which one.

blocks.content:
Load a sample query.

This one runs against **grafanacloud-play-prom**, a Prometheus data source holding metrics from a demo system. The query is written in PromQL, the language Prometheus understands, and it asks for the average response time of the demo's checkout service. That's your teammate's question, pointed at a service that actually exists here. You don't need to read PromQL yet, just know that the text box holds the question.

Click **Run query**.

This sends the query on the page to the data source and redraws the result below. The query already asks for response times, so to answer your teammate you'd only widen the time range to cover yesterday's release, then run it again.
blocks.tooltip: Sends the query on this page to the data source and redraws the result below.

blocks.content:
Read the chart below the query.

It draws the checkout service's response times, the very number your teammate asked about. If the line steps up at yesterday's release and stays up, your teammate was right. If it holds flat, the release is off the hook. Either way you have your answer, and it took one query.
blocks.tooltip: This is the result of the query above it, drawn the same way a dashboard panel would draw it.

blocks.content: You had one precise question, and Explore answered it without saving or building anything. Pick a data source, run a query, read the chart. That loop works for any question you can put into a query. When you can't, because all you know is that something looks wrong, that's an investigation, and the [guide on Drilldown](https://interactive-learning.grafana.net/guides/get-started-see-drilldown) shows you how to run one with clicks instead of queries.
